lines.li: [us] How are the lessons going?
[them,their:spacer] At home I'd learn this from a manual, here I learn it from a person.
[them,their:tribal] My hands are slow, but they are starting to remember.
[them] Slower than I'd like, but I can feel it sticking.
[us] Keep at it, it comes on its own one day.
[them] Is it normal to get things wrong this often when you're learning?
[us,trait:Kind] Of course, and the mistakes are where most of the learning is.
[us] Everyone here ruined something while they learned their trade.
[them] Then I'm learning a great deal.
[us] Why did your family send you here, of all places?
[them,their:empire] To learn a trade, which at court is thought very eccentric.
[them,their:tribal] So I would know how other people live, before I have to speak for ours.
[them] To learn what they couldn't teach me at home.
[us] And what do you want to learn?
[them] How to be useful, I think.
[us] You've gone quiet these last few days.
[them,their:tribal] I keep hearing my mother's voice calling us in at dusk.
[them,their:medieval] I keep thinking of the bells at home on a market day.
[them,their:hightech] I keep reaching for things that are back in my room at home.
[them] I keep thinking I hear my family in the next room.
[us] Come and work with me this afternoon, the time goes faster.
[them] I want to go home.
[us] I know, it's a long time to be away.
[them] Will they remember me?
[us] Every one of them, and they'll ask you a hundred questions.
[them] I know everyone's name now, and who snores.
[us] Then you know more than some who've been here for years.
[them] I had a lot of nights to listen.
[us] You're up and working before anyone has to tell you now.
[them] I'd rather be busy than sit thinking about home.
[us] That's how most of us got through our first season.
[them] I don't want the year to end.
[us] Then come back and see us when you're grown.
[them,their:empire] My family would never allow it, but I shall try.
[them] I'd like that, if my family lets me.
[them] Can I stay here forever?
[us] Your family would miss you too much.
[them] They could come here too.
[us] Ask them that when they come for you.
[them] What do you do when you're sad?
[us] Find something to do with my hands, usually.
[them] Can I do it with you?
[us] Of course you can.
[them] I'm better at lessons here than I was at home.
[us] Maybe you're older now.
[them] I'm much older.
[them] Is it always this lean here?
[us] Not always, it's been a hard few weeks.
[them] I won't complain, then, my family warned me it might be hard.
[them] I've never eaten as well as I have this month.
[us] Then you came to us in a good year.
[them] Is it always this loud with a new baby?
[us] {BORN} has good lungs, that's for certain.
[them] I'll sleep with my head under the blanket, then.
[them] I'd never seen a wedding outside my own people before.
[us] Was it so different?
[them,their:tribal] There was no shared fire, but the two of them looked just as happy.
[them] Less than I thought, the food and the crying were the same.
[them] At home we'd stay in on a day like this.
[us] Here the rain doesn't get a say.
[them] Winter's colder here than at home, or maybe I just notice it more.
[us] Away from home, everything's colder.
[them] That's what my grandmother said before I left.
[them] Your people have been kinder to me than I expected.
[us] What did you expect?
[them,their:lowtech] My uncles told stories about outsiders, and none of them were kind.
[them] Hard work and cold beds, mostly.
[us] Well, the work is hard.
[them] I didn't ask to be sent here, you know.
[us] Most of us didn't ask to be here either.
[them] That doesn't make it better.
[them] I promised {WARD}'s family I'd look in on them while I was here.
[us] Go and find them, they'll be glad of a face from home.
[them] I'll need to, or I'll never hear the end of it.
[them] We hear you work {WARD} like a hired hand.
[us] We work {WARD} like one of our own.
[them] That's what worries us.
[them] We heard about the raid, and the first thing anyone asked about was {WARD}.
[us] We keep {WARD} as safe as we keep our own.
[them] That's all a family can ask.
[them] {WARD}'s family talks about little else since the year began.
[us] {WARD} will have plenty to tell them.
[them,their:lowtech] Then the evenings at home will be long ones.
[them] Good, they're running out of things to guess at.
[us] Do your people often send their young ones away to learn?
[them,their:tribal] A child raised among another clan comes home with two families.
[them,their:medieval] A youth of a good house serves in another, it's how alliances are made.
[them,their:industrial] An apprenticeship under contract, and the contract runs a year.
[them,their:spacer,!their:empire] A posting on agreed terms, with a report at the end of it.
[them,their:empire] A page in a titled household learns more than any tutor can teach.
[them] Now and then, when there's a family we trust to take them.
[them] {WARD} sits with the elders some nights and asks them about the old days.
[us] That sounds like {WARD}.
[them] The elders like being asked, it doesn't happen often.
[them] {WARD} haggles at our market better than I do now.
[us] They didn't learn that from us.
[them] Then they learned it from our fishwives, and that's worse.
[them] {WARD} keeps a notebook of everything they're shown.
[us] Good, they'll need it when they're home.
[them] It's nearly full, and the year's not out.
[them] {WARD} has asked to see every machine in our town.
[us] Did you let them?
[them] Most of them, under supervision.
[us] Does {WARD} talk about home?
[them] Every evening, and about your cook in particular.
[us] Tell them the cook asks after them too.
[them] {WARD} works hard, I'll give them that.
[us] And?
[them] And asks too many questions about our business.
[them] Your page still bows too low, which the household finds charming.
[us] Better too low than not at all.
[them] At court, that depends entirely on whom one bows to.
[us] What does a page do all day?
[them] Carries things and keeps quiet, which is harder than it sounds.
[us] {WARD}, keeping quiet, I'd like to see that.
[them] It took a season, but the household is very patient.
[them] Is anyone still here from the year I spent with you?
[us] Ask around, someone will remember you.
[them] I'd like to thank whoever taught me.
[them,their:lowtech] When I lead my people, your colony will have a seat at our table.
[them] When I lead my people, I won't forget the year I spent here.
[us] We'll hold you to that.
[them] I watched your council argue all year and still get things done.
[us] Mostly argue, some days.
[them] I lead my own people now, and I think of it more than you'd guess.
[them] I remember my year here, and not all of it fondly.
[us] I'm sorry for the parts that weren't good.
[them] So am I.
